clue.text: Needing new blood right away for American administration

indicators.note: administration is read as a rearranging, the remaining letters being dispensed in a new order
away tells us to send the letter for right off from the word American

explanation.surface: A remark that a US government needs fresh blood straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes R from AMERICAN, leaving AMEICAN, and 'administration' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking red blood cells is said to need new blood, the sense of the medical adjective.

clue.text: Plug falling out and floating

parts.note: a plug is a promotion, an advert, shortened to AD
a falling out between friends is a rift

explanation.surface: A bath plug comes loose and drifts about in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat drifting with no mooring is floating free, the plain sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Hollow weapon, mine

parts.note: arms are weapons, so one weapon is an arm
a coal mine is a pit

explanation.surface: A hollowed-out weapon used as a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: The underarm is a hollow under the shoulder, so the body part is an example of a hollow.

clue.text: Roy in a position with girl on top? On the contrary

definitions.text: Roy in a position with girl on top? On the contrary

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top means the girl comes first, above the rest

parts.note: a girl is a miss

indicators.note: position is read as a verb, to place the letters of Roy in a in a new order

explanation.surface: A risque question about sexual positions with a woman uppermost, answered with a wink.
explanation.walkthrough: The missionary position famously puts the man on top, hence 'On the contrary': the clue's picture is the reverse of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The missionary position is the classic face-to-face sexual position with the man above, the reverse of girl on top.

clue.text: Move slowly with a stroke

definitions.meaning: to go at a snail's pace, as traffic or a baby does

explanation.definitionFit: Traffic is said to inch along at a snail's pace, and front crawl is a swimming stroke.

clue.text: Many take a leap, start off with a youngster

indicators.note: start off says the first letter of the leap word is dropped

parts.note: to take a leap is to jump
a youngster may be a teen

explanation.surface: Lots of people jump off with a young person.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word means a large but unspecified number, a synonym for lots.

clue.text: Introduced the woman in previously owned home

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a previously owned car is a used one
the woman, as a pronoun, is her
at home is in

explanation.surface: A woman shown into a second-hand house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal, while the final IN comes from 'home', as in staying at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To show a guest into a room is to introduce them, a close synonym of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: One seeking honey? Ring up stomach

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the ring word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a hoop is a ring
to stomach something is to bear it, to tolerate it

explanation.surface: Ring up and ask for something to settle the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne's bear is forever hunting honey, so the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Worthy and substantial one taken up by her in Paris

indicators.note: taken up by is read as absorbed by, so the turned letters go inside the French pronoun

parts.note: the French for she or her is elle

indicators.note: taken up, in a down clue, says the pieces read upwards

parts.note: something substantial is big
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A worthy and well-off man adopted by a woman in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' is a reversal in a down clue, and 'by' then reads as 'absorbed by': the turned letters sit inside the French word for she.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitable or qualified person is worthy of selection, as in an eligible bachelor.

clue.text: 50% excess included in futile and inadequate defence

indicators.note: included in puts those letters inside the futile phrase

parts.note: something futile is of no use, written as NO USE

indicators.note: 50% says half the letters of excess are taken, its first half

explanation.surface: An excessive and futile plea that fails as a defence.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying there is no excuse for something is to rule out any justification, a weak defence.

clue.text: Frolics without extremes are for politicians

indicators.note: without extremes strips the first and last letters from each of the next two words

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Politicians in favour of fun and games.
explanation.definitionFit: Romps are boisterous bouts of play, synonyms for frolics as plural nouns.

clue.text: The goddess of hairstyle heard to have a quirky diet

indicators.note: heard says the hairstyle is spoken, giving a word with the same sound but different spelling

parts.note: an Afro is a bushy hairstyle

indicators.note: quirky means odd, so the letters of diet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A goddess with a fancy hairdo is rumoured to follow an odd diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' gives APHRO, sounding like AFRO; 'quirky' makes DITE from DIET.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite was the Greek deity of love and beauty, so she is an example of a goddess.

clue.text: One may have a flutter up to the point of entry into a monastery

indicators.note: of entry into says the till word goes inside the monastery word

parts.note: a friary is a monastery of friars
till means up to the point in time, until

explanation.surface: Someone betting on the way into a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flutter' suggests a bet; here it is the flapping of a butterfly's wings.
explanation.definitionFit: The fritillary is a butterfly, and butterflies flutter their wings.

clue.text: An element of jazz in concert

indicators.note: of says the answer is a run of letters taken from the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of jazz music played live.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'An' alone as the definition; the definition is 'An element', with 'of' signalling the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a metallic chemical element, atomic number 30.

clue.text: Third of lesbian feminists get ugly, with head shaved in a way that's anything but 21 26

definitions.text: in a way that's anything but 21 26

indicators.note: Third of picks the third letter of lesbian

parts.note: wimmin is a spelling used by some feminists to avoid men in women

indicators.note: head shaved removes the first letter of ugly

explanation.surface: A provocative portrait of militant feminists turning ugly and shaving their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 26 is HARD GOING, so the definition means easily or smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: Things going smoothly are going with no difficulty, the opposite of a struggle.

clue.text: Deer suffering with swollen bums

indicators.note: suffering is read as being in a bad way, so the letters are put into disarray

explanation.surface: Deer in pain with swollen backsides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges DEER with SWOLLEN; 'bums' is not backsides but layabouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Bums in the sense of idle good-for-nothings are wastrels, a synonym for the plural noun.

clue.text: River crustacean the French find repugnant

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
a crab is a crustacean
the French for the is le

explanation.surface: French diners find a crab from a river disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means utterly dreadful, so it is a synonym for repugnant.

clue.text: Bird getting close, close to transport vessel

parts.note: nigh means close or near

indicators.note: close to picks the final letter of transport

parts.note: a jar is a vessel

explanation.surface: A bird nearing a ship for transport.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal bird, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Once more says that parts of corset are tight, when standing

indicators.note: when standing, in a down clue, says the hidden letters are read upwards
parts of says the answer's letters are taken from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A repeated complaint that a corset pinches.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'that parts'; 'parts of' is the hidden-run signal and 'that' a link, so the definition is 'Once more says'.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something again is to repeat it, the same verb in third person singular.

clue.text: Merge in turn is ordered when there's a gap at the top

definitions.text: when there's a gap at the top

indicators.note: ordered says the letters are rearranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: An instruction to merge traffic lanes in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: An interregnum is the period between two reigns, when no ruler holds the throne.

clue.text: Kilo for mile, yacht cover would do for the sunbather

indicators.note: for says one letter stands in place of the other

parts.note: a bimini is a canvas sunshade over a yacht's cockpit
K is kilo, in the NATO alphabet and as a prefix abbreviation

explanation.surface: Swapping units, a boat's awning becomes something to sunbathe in.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit, the sort of garment a sunbather wears.

clue.text: President whose age ran out

indicators.note: out is read as wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A president whose time ran out.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronald Reagan was the oldest US president at his inauguration, which gives the surface its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the 40th President of the United States, an example of the title.

clue.text: It's tough for Spooner's warder working in the garden

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped, as Rev Spooner did

parts.note: a prison warder is a guard
to work the soil with a hoe is hoeing

explanation.surface: A remark that a prison officer's gardening job is tough.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of GUARD and HOEING to get HARD GOING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard going is difficult and tiring, so the phrase means it's tough.

clue.text: Incinerate decomposing waste product

indicators.note: decomposing says the word breaks down and its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Burning rotting refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Creatinine is a breakdown product of muscle metabolism excreted in urine, a bodily waste.

clue.text: Minor mutation in angelfish

annotationWithheld.why: Minor mutation in angelfish (5): the blog's parse takes ANGEL* from 'angelfish' and 'fish' as the definition, so one clue word gives both fodder and definition, which no leaf can split.

clue.text: See 6
Dance with ale served first to last in pitcher

indicators.note: in says the moved ale goes inside the pitcher

parts.note: a pitcher is a jug

indicators.note: served first to last says the opening letter of the ale goes to the end

parts.note: bitter is a kind of English ale

explanation.surface: Dancing with a pitcher of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British pub beer, a hoppy ale; 'served first to last' moves its opening letter to the end before it goes in the pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The jitterbug is a lively swing dance of the 1940s.

clue.text: See 21
Ickle book?

parts.note: ickle is pickle missing its first letter; take that same letter from a longer word meaning to pickle food, and a verb meaning to book is left

explanation.surface: A tiny book, in baby talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ickle' looks like baby talk for little, but it stands for a pickling word that has lost its opening P; the clue asks for the same trick on a synonym of pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve a table is to book it in advance, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See Swansea girl being heavenly

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is a cathedral city in England
Sian is a Welsh girl's name, and Swansea is a city in Wales

explanation.surface: Looking at a Welsh girl and finding her divine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elysian Fields were the Greek paradise, so the adjective means blissful or of paradise.
